1.title: Sensitive Data, Secrets, Ephemeral Values and Write-Only Arguments
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Sensitive Data, Secrets, Ephemeral Values and Write-Only Arguments. It covers the exam area four. Terraform configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Sensitive values. Best practices for secrets. Hashi Corp Vault with Terraform. Ephemeral values. Write-only arguments. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Terraform configuration. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: Sensitive values
1.text: Sensitive values. Marking a variable or output sensitive true hides it in C L I output (shown as sensitive value ). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Sensitive values, continued
1.text: Sensitive values. What it hides. The value in plan and apply output and in terraform output. What it does not hide. The value is still stored in the state file and in saved plan files, in plain text. Derived values. A value built from a sensitive value must also be marked sensitive. Reading it anyway. terraform output -json or the state can show it to someone with access. Exam tip: sensitive hides, it does not encrypt. Protect the state and plan files as secrets.

1.title: Best practices for secrets
1.text: Best practices for secrets. Never hard-code secrets in dot tf files. They end up in version control. Do not commit terraform dot tfvars with secrets. Same reason. Supply secrets from the environment: T F var name or provider variables such as A W S A C C E S S K E Y I D. Not written to files. Use a secrets manager such as Hashi Corp Vault. Central, audited, rotated secrets. Prefer short-lived and dynamic credentials. A leaked value expires quickly. Encrypt and restrict the state. The state may contain secrets.

1.title: HashiCorp Vault with Terraform
1.text: Hashi Corp Vault with Terraform. Vault is a secrets management product. Terraform can read secrets from Vault with the Vault provider and a data source. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: HashiCorp Vault with Terraform, continued
1.text: Hashi Corp Vault with Terraform. Authentication. A token or other method, supplied through V A U L T T O K E N or provider settings, not hard-coded. The catch. A secret read through a data source is stored in the state. Better. Dynamic secrets from Vault (short-lived credentials), and ephemeral values (next sections). Exam tip: Reading a secret from Vault into an ordinary attribute still puts it in the state. Ephemeral values and write-only arguments were added to avoid that.

1.title: Ephemeral values (new in 004)
1.text: Ephemeral values (new in four). An ephemeral value exists only during the run and is never saved in the plan or the state.

1.title: Ephemeral values (new in 004), continued
1.text: Ephemeral values (new in four). The figure shows this: Ordinary values are saved in state and plan; ephemeral values are not.

1.title: Ephemeral values (new in 004), continued
1.text: Ephemeral values (new in four). Ephemeral input variable. ephemeral true in a variable block. Ephemeral resource. An ephemeral block that opens a temporary resource such as a generated password or a secret fetched at run time. Ephemeral output. In a child module, ephemeral true in an output block.

1.title: Ephemeral values (new in 004), continued
1.text: Ephemeral values (new in four). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Ephemeral values (new in 004), continued
1.text: Ephemeral values (new in four). Where an ephemeral value may be used: provider configuration, write-only arguments, other ephemeral contexts. Terraform refuses to use one in an ordinary resource argument, because that would save it in state.

1.title: Write-only arguments (new in 004)
1.text: Write-only arguments (new in four). A write-only argument is a resource argument that accepts a value, uses it and never stores it in the plan or state. By convention its name ends in wo, and a companion wo version argument tells Terraform when to send a new value. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Write-only arguments (new in 004), continued
1.text: Write-only arguments (new in four). Stored in state? No; the value is never saved. How to change it. Change the wo version number, so Terraform sends the new value again. Combine with. Ephemeral values, so the secret never touches the state. Exam tip: Ephemeral equals not saved. Write-only argument equals accepts an ephemeral value and does not store it. wo version is how you trigger an update.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A variable is marked sensitive. Where can its value still be found? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: In the state file, in plain text. Sensitive values are hidden in C L I output but remain in state and in saved plans.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. What is the best way to supply a database password to a configuration that is stored in version control? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Pass it through an environment variable or a secrets manager. Secrets should come from the environment or a secrets manager, not from files in version control.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A configuration reads a secret from Vault through a data source and uses it in an ordinary argument. What is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The secret is stored in the state. Values read through a data source and used in ordinary arguments are saved in state.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which value is never saved in the plan or the state? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: An ephemeral value. Ephemeral values exist only during the run and are not persisted.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What is a write-only argument? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An argument that accepts a value without storing it in the plan or state. A write-only argument uses the value but never saves it.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. How can a team make Terraform send a new value for a write-only password argument? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Change the matching wo version value. The companion version argument signals Terraform to send the new value again.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Does sensitive encrypt a value in the state? Answer: No, it only hides it in C L I output. Question two. Name one good way to supply a secret. Answer: An environment variable or a secrets manager. Question three. Which provider reads secrets from Vault? Answer: The Vault provider.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Where are ephemeral values stored? Answer: Nowhere; they are not saved in plan or state. Question five. What does a write-only argument name usually end in? Answer: wo. Question six. What does wo version do? Answer: Triggers sending a new write-only value.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. sensitive: hides in C L I output; still in state and plans. Secrets: never hard-code; environment or secrets manager; short-lived credentials. Vault: Vault provider and data sources; data source values land in state. Ephemeral: not saved: variables, resources, child module outputs. Write-only: wo arguments take ephemeral values and are not stored; wo version triggers updates.
